cd /Users/carter/dev/approval-md/.claude/worktrees/aprv-125-verbs && git add SPEC.md && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
APRV-125: SPEC §10.1 amendment — the two log verbs, the reconcile rule, no event

Adds `log sync` and `log advance` to the CLI block and states the three things
that are normative rather than incidental:

The reconcile rule. The committed chain must be a prefix of the working
snapshot, equal to it, or an extension of it; anything else is a fork the verb
must refuse, naming both heads and the first divergent seq. Implementations MUST
NOT merge or re-chain two chains under any circumstance, because re-chaining
fabricates records nobody wrote. Projections rebuild from the reconciled log and
are never restored from before the pull.

The prohibition on routing the log through git state mutation, `git stash`
included, and on `log advance` checking anything out.

The no-event decision: neither verb appends a record. The log records decisions
with real-world consequence, and moving the file the log is stored in is
housekeeping on the container — an event for it would be the log narrating its
own filesystem.

Closes with "(Amended APRV-125, pending sign-off.)" per the convention; the
awaiting-sign-off sentence above it is extended to name the pair.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
